notes: Stop now actually stops the render, and the UI returns to a ready state so you can start fresh without refreshing. Before, Stop killed only the shell (SIGTERM to `spawn('npx', …, { shell: true })`), so the underlying remotion/Chrome render kept running in the background and then popped 'video ready' — and the success path emitted render-done even after a cancel. Fixes: (server) new killTree() signals the whole process group; both the render-only audio/video spawns and the batch runProc spawn now use { detached: true } so each child is a group leader and the negative-PID SIGTERM (escalating to SIGKILL after 4s) reaches the entire tree (sh → npx → node → remotion → Chrome workers); added _renderOnlyCancelled checkpoints after the audio step and after the video render so a stopped run never renames out/1.mp4 or emits render-done; cancel-render and the batch cancelHandler now call killTree. (client) cancelRender shows 'Stopping…' then a 5s safety-net timeout calls a shared forceResetRenderUI() so the button frees itself even if the server never confirms; render-cancelled reuses forceResetRenderUI; render-done now ignores a stray/late completion that arrives after Stop (both active flags already cleared) so no ghost 'video ready'. NOTE: server.js is included in files[] — the in-app updater downloads it, but because apply-update only re-listens (doesn't re-exec node), the server half takes effect after a full app restart; the client half applies on reload. Verified: killTree terminates a detached shell + child sleepers (treeFullyKilled); client Stop→Stopping→ready, safety-net recovers UI with no server confirm, stray render-done ignored, legit render-done still shows modal; no console errors.
